official.description: Each year the Australian National University offers the University Research Scholarship to support high achieving HDR students conducting research which aligns with the strategic directions of the University. ANU conducts two annual central scholarship rounds which include the University Research Scholarship, RTP, and a few other centrally managed scholarships, and no separate application is required as all eligible candidates are considered based on their admission application.
official.program_type: Academic - centrally managed scholarship round, academic merit selection base

verification.notes: Stipend value ($40,475 p.a., 2027 full-time base rate), payment duration, allowances, eligibility, selection criteria and round deadlines were confirmed directly on ANU's official scholarship page. The page publishes no English test score and no statement that tuition fees are covered, so those fields are null.

applicant_utility.summary: The University Research Scholarship is ANU's stipend for research-degree students with at least an H1 (or equivalent), awarded automatically through the central rounds when you apply for admission, so your real deadline is the admission round deadline, not a separate scholarship form. Contact a prospective supervisor or HDR Convener early, because supervisor support and the research location are scored in the ranking. The domestic Round 1 deadline was moved to 26 October 2026 after a systems outage, so check the page again before you assume 31 October still applies.
applicant_utility.best_fit: H1/Honours graduates targeting a PhD or MPhil at ANU who need a living stipend and relocation support and can hit the central round deadlines.
application_readiness_checklist: Lodge the HDR admission application well before the round deadline and select 'Australia: ANU - Other Scholarship'
Nominate referees immediately so their reports arrive before the scholarship deadline
Email a prospective supervisor or HDR Convener to discuss the research topic before applying
If already an ANU student (under 1 year FTE), lodge the current-student scholarship consideration form
common_rejection_risks: Incomplete applications: referee reports not submitted by the scholarship deadline remove the application from the ranking entirely
Missing the round deadline, since late applications roll to the next round and delay commencement by months
Forgetting to select the 'Australia: ANU - Other Scholarship' option, which is what triggers consideration for all centrally managed scholarships
Weak evidence of research potential or supervisor support relative to other H1 applicants in the same round
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The official page does not state that tuition fees are covered by this scholarship (tuition relief comes through the separately awarded RTP), and the stipend is fixed, so living costs beyond the $40,475 p.a. stipend and any fees not offset by other awards must be self-funded.
document_audit: Referee reports are only triggered when you submit the admission application - there is no way to add them late before the deadline
Current ANU students need an extra form that admissions applicants do not need
Applications must be complete, including all supporting documentation, by the scholarship deadline, not just the admission deadline
alerts: Domestic Round 1 deadline for commencement by 30 March 2027 was changed from 31 October to 26 October 2026 (11.59pm) due to a scheduled outage - do not rely on the old date
International Round 1 deadline (31 August) is months earlier than the domestic one; international applicants work to a much tighter cycle
Round 2 only supports commencement by end of August in the same year, so missing Round 1 can cost nearly a year
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Submit one HDR admission application with the scholarship option ticked and referees nominated, ANU Colleges rank complete H1 applications, and outcomes follow in the central round - there is no separate scholarship application step.

official.description: The University of Sydney International Stipend Scholarship (USYDIS) is a competitively awarded scholarship for international students commencing or enrolled in a higher degree by research, paying a stipend of $44,293 p.a. at the 2027 rate plus relocation and thesis allowances, with holders automatically awarded the companion University of Sydney Tuition Fee Scholarship covering 100% of tuition fees for up to 14 research periods.
official.program_type: Higher degree by research scholarship, competitively awarded

verification.notes: The $44,293 p.a. (2027 rate) stipend, automatic tuition fee scholarship, preference criteria, application route and the full application and award timeline were confirmed on the University of Sydney's official RTP international page; relocation allowance amounts, claims rules and required documents were confirmed on the official RTP FAQs. No English test score or stipend duration is published on the scholarship pages, so those fields are null.

applicant_utility.summary: USYDIS is the University of Sydney's full funding package for international research students: a $44,293 p.a. stipend (2027 rate) plus automatic full tuition coverage for up to 14 research periods, but you must apply for admission and submit the scholarship form by a fixed round deadline. Late submissions are not lost - they roll into the next round automatically - but outcomes for the current round are already locked, so choose the round that matches your intended commencement date. Build your application around research evidence, because selection is on academic merit and research potential only, and second-class honours cannot be argued up to first class even with mitigating circumstances.
applicant_utility.best_fit: International students with a strong research record (ideally first-class honours or peer-reviewed publications) targeting a PhD or research master's at the University of Sydney who need tuition plus a living stipend.
application_readiness_checklist: Lodge the HDR course application through Sydney Courses first and keep the SID/IPU number handy for the scholarship form
Merge transcripts, grading system information and official translations into a single PDF before starting the form
Prepare research experience evidence on the University's template if you have publications or research roles
Target the round whose submission deadline matches your intended commencement research period
common_rejection_risks: Missing the round submission deadline, which pushes assessment into the next round and delays any outcome by months
Applying for the scholarship without the admission application - scholarship applications are assessed only in conjunction with admission
Weak or non-compliant research experience evidence: publications must be original, peer-reviewed and accepted by Scopus, ISI or ERA-listed sources, and self-published work is not accepted
Second-class honours results, which the University explicitly will not reclassify as first class even under mitigating circumstances
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Relocation support is capped at AUD $1,485 per claim with only two claims (start and end of degree) and excludes meals, accommodation and quotations, so most travel and shipping costs above the cap, plus living costs beyond the stipend and any dependants' costs, must be self-funded.
document_audit: Transcripts, grading scales and certified translations must all be combined into one PDF or the application is incomplete
The research experience form must be in the required format or it will not be considered
A publication accepted after submission requires resubmitting the whole scholarship application - and resubmitting after the deadline defers assessment to the next round
Conditional offers stall until final transcripts and grading scales are supplied

applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Apply for admission via Sydney Courses, submit the scholarship application form by the round deadline, then wait for the committee ranking - results release in batches from the published outcomes date and finalisation can take months for on-shore applicants.
